content: The International Code of Conduct on Pesticide Management: Guidance on Pesticide Legislation (Second Edition) was published in 2020 by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations and the World Health Organization (WHO). This document provides comprehensive guidance on the development and implementation of pesticide legislation, emphasizing the importance of effective regulatory frameworks to manage pesticides throughout their lifecycle. The publication clarifies that the designations and presentation of material do not imply any legal or developmental status of countries, territories, or regions, nor do they endorse specific companies or products. The views expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect the policies of FAO or WHO. The document is available under a Creative Commons license, allowing non-commercial use with proper citation, but prohibits the use of FAO or WHO logos. The guidance emphasizes the importance of aligning pesticide legislation with international agreements, such as the Rotterdam Convention, Stockholm Convention, Basel Convention, Montreal Protocol, and others. It also underscores the need for countries to harmonize their laws with non-binding international guidelines, such as the Code of Conduct, to address emerging challenges like antimicrobial resistance and environmental contamination. The document outlines the critical components of pesticide legislation, including primary laws (acts or ordinances) and secondary regulations (rules, decrees, or notices). It stresses the importance of a unified legal framework that covers all aspects of pesticide management, from manufacturing and distribution to use and disposal. The publication highlights the progress made since the adoption of the original Code of Conduct in 1985, noting that most countries now have some form of pesticide legislation. However, many existing laws are outdated, lack alignment with international standards, or fail to address new priorities. Common issues include unclear responsibilities, weak enforcement mechanisms, and insufficient integration with other relevant legislation, such as environmental protection or food safety laws. The guidance provides a step-by-step process for drafting or revising pesticide legislation, including analyzing national legal and institutional frameworks, identifying technical needs, drafting laws with input from legal and technical experts, and involving stakeholders in the review process. It emphasizes the importance of tailoring legislation to national circumstances, such as local agricultural practices, pest problems, and socioeconomic conditions. The document also discusses the broader regulatory framework for pesticide management, which may include laws on environmental protection, public health, occupational safety, and international trade. It recommends that pesticide legislation be as comprehensive as possible, covering all stages of the pesticide lifecycle and ensuring consistency with national legal systems and international obligations. Finally, the guidance encourages governments to strengthen institutional infrastructure, promote integrated pest and vector management, and provide training and education to stakeholders. It underscores the need for clear enforcement provisions and adequate resources to achieve compliance and protect public health and the environment.
